question: On a motorway at night you see red reflective road studs on your left. What do they mark?
options: The left edge of the carriageway
A contraflow lane
The central reservation
A slip road
explanation: Reflective road studs may be used with white lines. White studs mark the lanes or the middle of the road; red studs mark the left edge of the road; amber studs mark the central reservation of a dual carriageway or motorway; green studs mark the edge of the main carriageway at lay-bys and slip roads; green/yellow studs indicate temporary adjustments to lane layouts. (Highway Code rule 132.)

question: Which of these MUST NOT use a motorway?
options: A car with L plates driven under qualified supervision in a dual-control vehicle
A motorcycle with an engine capacity under 50 cc
A car towing a trailer
A motorhome
explanation: Prohibited vehicles. Motorways MUST NOT be used by pedestrians, holders of provisional motorcycle or car licences (unless accompanied by an approved driving instructor in a dual-controlled car), riders of motorcycles under 50 cc, cyclists, horse riders, certain slow-moving vehicles, agricultural vehicles and powered wheelchairs/mobility scooters. (Highway Code rule 253.)

question: Holders of a provisional car licence may drive on a motorway only if…
options: They are over 21
They are accompanied by an approved driving instructor in a car fitted with dual controls
They display L plates and drive below 60 mph
They have passed the theory test
explanation: Prohibited vehicles. Motorways MUST NOT be used by pedestrians, holders of provisional motorcycle or car licences (unless accompanied by an approved driving instructor in a dual-controlled car), riders of motorcycles under 50 cc, cyclists, horse riders, certain slow-moving vehicles, agricultural vehicles and powered wheelchairs/mobility scooters. (Highway Code rule 253.)

question: On a motorway, red lights are flashing above your lane and a red “X” is shown. What MUST you do?
options: Do not drive in that lane beyond the signal
Reduce speed to 50 mph in that lane
Continue but be prepared to stop
Move into that lane to leave others clear
explanation: If red lights flash on a signal and a red 'X' is showing, you MUST NOT drive in the lane shown as closed beyond the signal. If red lights flash on a signal in the central reservation or at the side of the road and lane closed sign is displayed, you MUST NOT go beyond the signal in any lane. (Highway Code rule 257.)

question: When joining a motorway from a slip road you should…
options: Force your way into the right-hand lane
Match your speed to the traffic in the left-hand lane and join when there is a safe gap
Use the hard shoulder to build up speed
Stop at the end of the slip road and wait for a gap
explanation: Joining the motorway. When you join the motorway you will normally approach it from a road on the left (a slip road) or from an adjoining motorway. You should give priority to traffic already on the motorway, check the traffic on the motorway and match your speed to fit safely into the traffic flow in the left-hand lane, not cross solid white lines that separate lanes, and stay on the slip road if it continues as an extra lane on the motorway. (Highway Code rule 259.)

question: You miss your intended exit on a motorway. What should you do?
options: Make a U-turn through the central reservation
Reverse along the hard shoulder to the exit
Carry on to the next exit
Stop and wait for a gap to cross to the exit
explanation: You MUST NOT reverse, cross the central reservation, or drive against the traffic flow on a motorway. If you have missed your exit, or have taken the wrong route, carry on to the next exit. (Highway Code rule 263.)

question: On a three-lane motorway with no traffic ahead, which lane should you normally drive in?
options: The left-hand lane
The right-hand lane
Whichever lane has the smoothest surface
The middle lane
explanation: Lane discipline. You should always drive in the left-hand lane when the road ahead is clear. If you are overtaking a number of slower-moving vehicles, you should return to the left-hand lane as soon as you are safely past. (Highway Code rule 264.)

question: On a three-lane motorway, which of these MUST NOT use the right-hand lane?
options: A car towing a trailer
A small van under 2 tonnes
A car carrying four passengers
A motorcycle over 125 cc
explanation: The right-hand lane of a motorway with three or more lanes MUST NOT be used (except in prescribed circumstances) by any vehicle drawing a trailer, a goods vehicle with a maximum laden weight exceeding 3.5 tonnes, a passenger vehicle with a maximum laden weight exceeding 7.5 tonnes, or a vehicle required to be fitted with a speed limiter. (Highway Code rule 265.)

question: In congested motorway traffic, the lane on your left is moving faster than yours. What does the Highway Code say?
options: You must change to the left lane to avoid undertaking
You may use the hard shoulder to keep moving
You may keep up with traffic in your lane even if it means passing vehicles on your right
You must slow down to match the right-hand lane
explanation: Overtaking. Do not overtake on the left or move to a lane on your left to overtake. In congested conditions, where adjacent lanes of traffic are moving at similar speeds, traffic in left-hand lanes may sometimes be moving faster than traffic to the right; in these conditions you may keep up with the traffic in your lane even if this means passing traffic in the lane to your right. (Highway Code rule 267.)

question: On a smart motorway, what does a speed limit shown above the hard shoulder mean?
options: You may stop on the hard shoulder for up to two minutes
You may use the hard shoulder as a running lane at that speed
The hard shoulder is closed to all traffic
Only HGVs may use the hard shoulder
explanation: Hard shoulder. You MUST NOT use the hard shoulder for overtaking. On some motorways the hard shoulder is used as a running lane: a red 'X' or blank signal above the hard shoulder means it is for emergency use only; a speed limit sign above means you may use it as a running lane. (Highway Code rule 269.)

question: When may you stop on a motorway hard shoulder?
options: To let a tired passenger drive
Only in an emergency, or when told to by police, traffic officers or signals
To check a map
To answer a phone call
explanation: You MUST NOT stop on the carriageway, hard shoulder, slip road, central reservation or verge except in an emergency, or when told to do so by the police, traffic officers, an emergency sign or by flashing red light signals. (Highway Code rule 270.)

question: When leaving a motorway, when should you signal left?
options: Only when you reach the slip road
In good time, after moving into the left-hand lane
At the 100-yard countdown marker only
You should not signal — the slip road makes it obvious
explanation: Leaving the motorway. Unless signs indicate that a lane leads directly off the motorway, you will normally leave by a slip road on your left. Watch for the signs letting you know you are getting near your exit, move into the left-hand lane well before reaching your exit, and signal left in good time. (Highway Code rule 272.)

question: After leaving a motorway, why should you check your speedometer?
options: It is required by law within one mile
To recalibrate cruise control
It may have been reset by the motorway signals
Your speed may be higher than you realise
explanation: On leaving the motorway or using a link road between motorways, your speed may be higher than you realise — 50 mph may feel like 30 mph. Check your speedometer and adjust your speed accordingly. (Highway Code rule 273.)

question: After a breakdown on the hard shoulder, how should you rejoin the motorway?
options: Reverse to the previous slip road
Pull straight out and accelerate hard
Wait for a flashing amber signal
Build up speed on the hard shoulder and join when there is a safe gap
explanation: To rejoin the carriageway after a breakdown from a hard shoulder, build up speed on the hard shoulder and watch for a safe gap in the traffic. Be aware that other vehicles may be stationary on the hard shoulder. (Highway Code rule 278.)
